program.notes: let_me_buy (letmebuy.app) — a storefront program: a merchant stands up a store, lists products, and buyers pay in an SPL token by scanning a QR code. ONE PDA per store carries everything: receipts = ['receipts', store_name] (store_name is an instruction ARGUMENT, utf8), and the account holds the products vec, the receipts vec, total_purchases, authority, telegram_channel_id, details and bump. Every one of the eight instructions takes that same account, writable — which is what makes the lifecycle a chain rather than eight unrelated calls, and why product_name is never a seed. Derivation order is trivial (receipts depends on nothing but the store name) and the two associated-token accounts depend only on caller-supplied owner/mint, so nothing here needs a chain read to build. Instruction account lists, in IDL order: initialize(store_name) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer), system_program]; add_product(store_name, name, price:u64) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer), mint, system_program]; make_purchase(store_name, product_name, table_number:u8) = [receipts(w), signer(w,signer), authority(w), mint, sender_token_account(w), recipient_token_account(w), token_program, system_program, associated_token_program] (9); mark_as_delivered(_store_name, receipt_id:u64) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]; update_details(store_name, details) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]; update_telegram_channel(store_name, telegram_channel_id) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]; delete_product(store_name, product_name) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer), system_program]; delete_store(store_name) = [receipts(w), authority(w,signer)]. THE JOIN THE IDL LOSES: mark_as_delivered's receipts account declares the seed arg path 'store_name', but that instruction's own args are named '_store_name' and 'receipt_id' — the seed points at an argument that does not exist in its instruction, so an IDL-driven deriver that resolves seed paths by arg name gets nothing for the one seed that selects the store. The recipe here binds by seed VALUE ('store_name' for all eight), and the wire arg for that call stays '_store_name'. SECOND TRAP: in make_purchase the store's `authority` is writable but NOT a signer — the merchant does not co-sign a sale; CORRECTED 2026-08-14: this note used to say the program checks it against receipts.authority (6004 InvalidAuthority). IT DOES NOT. That require! guard is present in add_product, update_details, update_telegram_channel, delete_product and delete_store, and ABSENT from make_purchase (verified against the program's source, Woody4618/bar, osec-matched to the deployed binary). The payee is derived from a caller-supplied key that nothing on chain validates, and PurchaseMade carries no recipient field — a fulfiller acting on that event cannot tell a paid order from an unpaid one. Mainnet 3YDcon1k… is a make_purchase with source == destination and IDENTICAL pre/post token balances that still returned success and emitted PurchaseMade. This is why the plan is checked HERE, against the authority read from the store's own account, rather than trusted to the program. THIRD TRAP, and the most load-bearing behavioural fact about this program: the receipts vec is CAPPED AT 20 and the account never reallocs (fixed at 3,681 bytes). At the cap make_purchase does receipts.remove(0) — the oldest receipt is SILENTLY EVICTED, with no error, no event and no log. jonasbar has 125 purchases and holds 20; 105 are gone from chain. Two consequences: mark_as_delivered on an evicted id SUCCEEDS AND DOES NOTHING (it scans the vec and returns Ok when it finds nothing), so a venue with more than 20 open orders loses them from the delivery queue invisibly; and compute is BOUNDED, not growing — CU rises ~12.7 per resident receipt byte until the cap and is bit-exact flat after it (CU ~= 19,780 + 12.7 x resident bytes, cross-validated across two stores to 0.9%). A shop never outgrows the transaction; it outgrows its own memory. The buyer pays from sender_token_account = ATA(signer, token_program, mint) and the store is credited at recipient_token_account = ATA(authority, token_program, mint) — same mint, same token program, different owner; deriving both from the same owner builds a purchase that pays the buyer back. token_program is pinned by the IDL to classic SPL Token (TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA), so both ATAs are classic-Token ATAs and a Token-2022 mint has no path through this program. The currency is fixed per product by add_product's `mint` account (stored with price and decimals in the products vec); a make_purchase whose mint differs fails 6003 InvalidMint. delete_store DOES NOT refuse a non-empty store — CORRECTED 2026-08-17, this note used to say it refuses one with products (6005 StoreNotEmpty) and delete_product must come first. Verified against the program source (Woody4618/bar, programs/let-me-buy/src/lib.rs:298): delete_store checks InvalidAuthority ONLY, then zeroes the receipts account's lamports and credits the authority — the account is closed whatever it holds. StoreNotEmpty is DECLARED in the error enum (lines 36-37) and RAISED NOWHERE in the program. Measured the same day: a simulated delete_store against a store listing two products and holding 20 receipts SUCCEEDED at 16,893 CU with clean logs. This is a general defect class an IDL-derived surface cannot see: an error code in the IDL's error table reads as a guarantee, and a declared-but-unraised code is a guarantee nothing enforces. A flow that trusts it deletes a live storefront and its history. FOURTH TRAP, and an IDL cannot show it: mark_as_delivered enforces NO AUTHORITY CHECK. Its `authority` account is declared writable+signer, which makes Anchor verify that SOMEBODY signed and never WHO, and the instruction body carries no require! against receipts.authority - the guard the same program does apply in add_product, update_details, update_telegram_channel, delete_product and delete_store. MEASURED 2026-08-17 on a surfpool mainnet fork: a keypair generated seconds earlier, with no relationship to the storefront and no cheatcode applied to it, landed mark_as_delivered against jonasbar and flipped receipt 126 to delivered - err null, 34,870 CU, logs ending 'Marked purchase as delivered 126 19'. So anyone can clear anyone's delivery queue for a 5,000-lamport fee, and a surface derived from the IDL reads `signer: true` as if it named WHICH signer. Reproduced by gecko/sandbox/deliver.py, rehearse_delivery(..., take_the_store=False). Other errors: 6001 ProductAlreadyExists, 6002 ProductNotFound, 6006 ProductNameEmpty, 6007 StringTooLong, 6008 VectorLimitReached, 6009 InvalidStoreName. PROVENANCE: the Anchor IDL that states these recipes reached comprehension through the hosted project surface (a third-party mirror), not from the program's own on-chain IDL account, and the seeds were hand-authored into this config from it — so every entry is carried at `manual`, the reviewed-overlay tier, rather than `extracted`. Correctness of the receipts recipe is established separately, by a derived address matching a mainnet account the program owns; that is a chain fact pinned in tests/test_let_me_buy_config.py, and it is evidence, never a tier. No execute intent is wired for this program yet: it is comprehended for DERIVATION only. STORE NAME (observed, not established from source): the program refuses at least one store_name with 6009 InvalidStoreName — 'gecko_coffee' was refused and 'geckocoffee' accepted in the same run — and the two differ by one underscore, which is not enough to state a rule, so none is stated here; see program.arg_constraints.store_name.

store_name.note: OBSERVED, NOT ESTABLISHED FROM SOURCE. The program rejects at least one store_name with error 6009 InvalidStoreName: 'gecko_coffee' was refused (6009, 14,202 CU) and 'geckocoffee' was accepted (8,014 CU) in the same $0 simulation run; 'jonasbar' is a store that exists on mainnet. The two tested names differ by ONE underscore, and two data points cannot tell 'no underscore' apart from 'alphanumeric only' or any other rule, so no rule is stated here. What the artifact does say: every instruction declares store_name as a bare `string` with no length, charset or pattern (an Anchor IDL cannot express one), and length has its OWN code — 6007 StringTooLong — so 6009 is not the too-long answer. Until the check is read from source, treat any store_name outside the accepted list as UNVERIFIED, not as invalid.
